topic: Abstention in the 2009 European Parliament election

desired_action.description: Vote in the 2009 European Parliament election
desired_action.actor_group: People eligible to vote in the European Parliament election
desired_action.time_horizon: During the 2009 European Parliament election period
desired_action.observable_success: An eligible person casts a ballot in the election

evidence.population: Focus-group participants discussing abstention from the 2009 European Parliament election
evidence.participant_count_note: The schema-required integer is a conservative lower bound for the three groups in one Member State (3 groups × the reported minimum of 8 participants), not the total study count. The source reports three groups per Member State and 8–12 participants per group; no overall participant total is asserted here.
evidence.sampling_method: Qualitative focus-group design with three groups per Member State and 8–12 participants per group; explicitly non-representative
evidence.moderator_prompt: The supplied source facts establish that the focus groups concerned abstention; exact moderator wording is not transcribed here.
evidence.theme: Reported themes included lack of knowledge or information about candidates and the European Parliament, and difficulty connecting EU-level politics with daily life.
limitations: The focus groups are explicitly non-representative; qualitative themes do not estimate how common views are in the population.
Group size was reported as a range of 8–12; participants_n is a conservative lower bound for one Member State's three groups, not an exact study total.
Themes are paraphrased from the report; no raw quotations or participant-level data are included.
The study was conducted three years after the 2009 survey, so the two evidence streams are not the same participant sample or time point.
evidence.source_title: ‘Impulsive’ and ‘Unspecified’ Abstainers: Voting Barriers and Incentives

evidence.population: Respondents who did not vote in the recent European Parliament elections
evidence.sampling_method: Face-to-face post-electoral survey conducted across the 27 EU Member States and coordinated by TNS Opinion & Social; this record retains the source's non-voter aggregate only
evidence.question: What are the main reasons why you did NOT vote in the recent European Parliament elections?
response_scale: Lack of trust/dissatisfaction with politics generally
Not interested in politics as such
Vote has no consequences/vote does not change anything
Do not know much about EU/EP/elections
Did not know there were elections
evidence.percentage_base: Respondents who did not vote in the recent European Parliament elections; this subgroup was 57% of the total sample.
limitations: Percentages are rounded reported values. Up to three answers were allowed, so the percentages are not expected to sum to 100% and have not been normalized.
The source facts provide no respondent count for this base; no respondent counts are inferred.
The denominator is non-voters (57% of the total sample), not the full survey sample.
Aggregate survey results describe reported reasons and do not establish individual motives or causal effects.
The 2012 qualitative study notes that the survey and focus groups are separated by time and use different methods; this record does not treat them as one sample.
